version: motion-3 · 2026-09-13 · window 75s · dwell 10s · cruise speed · decay 120s · horizon 120s
method: along-route extrapolation at the speed of the journey’s own recent reports, bounded in time, pausing 10 s at each timetabled stop it reaches, at the speed of the stretches where its reports show it moving, eased off as the report ages

params.version: motion-3 · 2026-09-13 · window 75s · dwell 10s · cruise speed · decay 120s · horizon 120s

fitted.maxSpeed: 99th percentile of along-route speed between consecutive training reports (6810 pairs)
fitted.speedWindow: the window, of 25, 45 and 75 s, with the lowest mean training error up to a minute
fitted.horizon: the longest run of report-age bins from the start in which the median training error beat the last report’s
fitted.family: dwell of 0, 6, 10, 15 or 20 s at each timetabled stop reached; speed from the whole window or from the moving stretches only (cruise); a bus shown standing held 0 or 15 s; decay of 0, 45, 60, 90 or 120 s: 200 candidates
fitted.rule: within 2% of the best mean training error up to a minute, the candidate whose arriving reports move the estimate least on average; chosen before any held-out figure was read

notes: Scored only against reports that arrived. Sparse reports, about 20 s apart, cannot check a drawn position between two of them.
The baseline is the last report itself, which is what the page draws without estimates.
These scores are for the estimate. While a correction settles, the drawn bus trails it, catching up no faster than a set rate.
An estimate never becomes an observation: none of these is stored or published as a position.
